title: Modular regression testing framework built on AWS for large-scale systems
summary: Regression testing must catch behavior changes before they reach production, yet synthetic tests miss real-world edge cases. This post walks through a modular framework, built on AWS, that replays a sample of production traffic against new code and automatically gates deployments on the fraction of results that match production.

title: Scale distributed AI workloads with Ray and Anyscale on Amazon EC2
summary: Building multimodal AI/ML pipelines on Amazon EC2 means scaling distributed compute, controlling costs across stages, and keeping up with new models and hardware. This post shows how the Ray-powered Anyscale application on AWS helps you deploy Ray across three compute options and scale from prototype to production without code changes.

title: Inside an enterprise AI agent: A governed, observable loop architecture
summary: This post lays out a five-layer reference architecture for governed, observable enterprise AI agents on AWS: an API gateway, a five-phase agent runtime, a knowledge and state tier, platform services, and a cross-cutting trust and control framework. Each layer maps to managed AWS services, with the design patterns worth copying and the mistakes to avoid.

title: Validating your DR commitment: From controlled test to real-world readiness
summary: After you define your DR targets, testing tells you whether they hold. Part 2 of a three-part series.

title: Three business decisions that define your DR success
summary: A disaster recovery strategy is only as strong as the business decisions behind it. Before you choose an architecture pattern, three decisions shape whether recovery succeeds: what you're actually recovering, what the business needs from that recovery, and what your dependencies allow you to commit to. Part 1 of a three-part series.

title: Automating the full AWS DRS agent lifecycle: Install, heal, and offboard
summary: Keeping a large Amazon EC2 fleet continuously recoverable with AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery is a lifecycle challenge. This post shows how to automate the full DRS agent lifecycle (install, heal, and offboard) using AWS Systems Manager Automation and Amazon EventBridge, driven by a single EC2 tag and no Lambda functions.
